title: Q-Capsule: A Localized Capsule-Based Quantum Neural Architecture for Barren Plateau Mitigation
authors: Awal Ahmed Fime, Tasfia Zaman Samiha, Saika Zaman, Dimitris Pados, George Sklivanitis, Abdur R. Shahid, Ahmed Imteaj
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms are often limited by barren plateaus: gradients vanish as circuit size and depth increase, making quantum neural networks difficult to train. We propose Q-Capsule, a localized capsule-based quantum neural architecture that mitigates this problem through register partitioning, local readout, sparse inter-capsule coupling, trainable data re-uploading, and Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM)-guided adaptive depth growth. By restricting the dominant support of each observable to a small capsule and controlling inter-capsule entanglement, Q-Capsule preserves useful gradient signals while retaining communication between local quantum representations. As the register width increases, Q-Capsule consistently maintains stable gradient variance, whereas globally entangling baselines exhibit exponential suppression with a log-gradient-variance slope near -ln 2 per qubit. Q-Capsule also produces more structured optimization landscapes, higher parameter efficiency, improved robustness to depolarizing noise, and lower measurement requirements. Its adaptive policy achieves 98.1% accuracy on binary classification and 97.7% on four-class classification, while using approximately 73% fewer two-qubit gates than the fixed-deep model on the multiclass task.
summary: This paper introduces Q-Capsule, a novel quantum neural network architecture designed to overcome the barren plateau problem plaguing VQAs. It achieves this by localizing quantum computations into interconnected 'capsules' and adaptively controlling circuit depth using the QFIM. The resulting model maintains stable gradient signals while achieving high classification accuracy with significantly fewer required quantum gates.
main_problem: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are severely limited by the barren plateau phenomenon, where gradients vanish exponentially as the quantum circuit size or depth increases, making training difficult.
main_result: Q-Capsule mitigates barren plateaus by using localized capsule structures and sparse coupling, maintaining stable gradient variance even as the total number of qubits increases.
method: The authors propose Q-Capsule, a localized capsule-based quantum neural architecture that employs register partitioning, local readout, and Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM)-guided adaptive depth growth.
model_or_system: The model is a Quantum Neural Network (QNN) implemented via VQAs on a quantum register. It partitions the register into fixed-width 'capsules' which process information locally before sparsely interacting.
key_observables: Gradient variance ($	ext{Var}[\partial	heta\langle O_cangle]$), Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM), inter-capsule entanglement, and classification accuracy.
important_parameters: Capsule width ($c_{size}$), coupling interval ($k$), and the QFIM-derived expressibility score ($S_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that restricting observables to small capsules controls gradient concentration, and the adaptive growth uses a block-diagonal metric-tensor approximation of the QFIM.
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides an architectural overview, detailing the qubit partitioning, local readout mechanisms, and the pattern of intra-capsule and inter-capsule coupling.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the Q-Capsule architecture, presents detailed analysis of its mechanisms (including QFIM guidance), and concludes with performance metrics and future work directions.
why_interesting: The focus on gradient stability and structured local computation directly addresses fundamental limitations in scaling quantum machine learning models, which is crucial for developing practical quantum algorithms.

N denotes the total number of qubits, c the capsule index, csize the number of qubits per capsule, and Nc = N/csize the total number of capsules. k denotes the inter-capsule coupling interval. H is the Hadamard gate, Ry performs trainable data re-uploading, and Rot denotes a general trainable single-qubit rotation composed of Rx, Ry, and Rz. Blue control–target symbols denote intra-capsule CNOTs, orange symbols denote sparse inter-capsule CNOTs, gray symbols indicate capsule-dependent coupling determined by the alternating coupling pattern, and the green meter symbol denotes local capsule-wise measurement.
